title: BulkDestructiveFlow
summary: A recipe, not a component: "Delete 37 leads" confirms a bulk deletion with a sample and its consequences, asks for the count to be typed, runs it with a progress bar while the sheet is locked, then reports the items that failed.
whenToUse: When a bulk action deletes or changes many records at once and cannot be undone: delete selected leads, remove members, purge files.
whenNotToUse: For one item, use a confirm dialog. For an action that can be undone, run it at once and offer Undo in a snackbar. For a reversible archive, use MonarchBulkActionBar alone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, fullyExpanded: Boolean = true, fullWidthContent: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchBottomSheetScope.() -> Unit)
@Composable fun MonarchConsequenceList(items: List<MonarchConsequence>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, heading: String? = null, …)
@Composable fun MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase: String, value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, …)
@Composable fun MonarchProgress(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, progress: Float? = null, variant: MonarchProgressVariant = MonarchProgressVariant.Linear, label: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchBanner(message: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, title: String? = null, …, announcement: MonarchBannerAnnouncement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.None)

states.name: confirm
states.description: The title with the count, a sample of three names and "+34 more", the consequences, a field asking for the count, and a danger button disabled until the count matches.

states.name: running
states.description: A linear MonarchProgress with "12 of 37 deleted"; the sheet cannot be swiped or dismissed.

states.name: done
states.description: A success banner when every item was deleted, announced politely.

states.name: partial
states.description: A warning banner with "36 of 37 leads deleted" and the items that failed; the app can offer a retry for those items.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet in the colors Monarch maps to the scheme, holding Monarch parts: a heading, body text, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, a danger MonarchButton, a linear MonarchProgress and a success or warning MonarchBanner. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web BulkDestructiveFlow is a component built on WizardDialog with plural rules, a typeCountAbove threshold, an optional step-up authentication and a retry step. On Android it composes existing parts in a MonarchBottomSheet, so the app decides the threshold for typing the count, writes plural forms with plurals resources, and runs re-authentication (for example BiometricPrompt, which needs androidx.biometric in the app) before the deletion. The web's progress callback is the app's own loop updating a counter. The sheet is locked with dismissible = false while it runs. iOS uses the same recipe with a sheet.
accessibility: The title is a heading; MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed count matches, and the delete button stays disabled until it does.
MonarchProgress exposes its range and value, so TalkBack can follow "12 of 37 deleted".
The result banner is a polite live region, so the result is announced when the run ends without moving focus.
edgeCases: Lock the sheet with dismissible = false while the deletion runs, so it cannot be dismissed half way.
Keep the failed items selected after Done so the person can retry or inspect them.
If nothing could be deleted (the request failed), show the error in the confirm phase and keep the typed count.
